title: Isoler Goose avec GOOSE_PATH_ROOT pendant les évaluations locales
description: Rediriger toutes les écritures Goose du tooling et de l'Eval Hub vers leur fakeroot afin d'éviter les mutations de ~/.local/share/goose.
design: Conserver XDG_CONFIG_HOME/goose comme source utilisateur uniquement. Utiliser GOOSE_PATH_ROOT comme destination effective dans les deux implémentations de sandbox.
acceptance_criteria: GOOSE_PATH_ROOT pointe vers $HARNESS_SANDBOX_ROOT/goose; config.yaml, custom_* et OAuth sont installés sous $GOOSE_PATH_ROOT/config; data et state restent privés; tous les processus Goose héritent de la variable; les tests ciblés passent; les chemins utilisateur réels restent surveillés.
notes: GOOSE_PATH_ROOT isole tooling et Eval Hub sous le fakeroot. Preuves: tooling sandbox 15/15; Eval Hub sandbox/release gate 17/17; builds TypeScript tooling et eval-hub réussis; vérification indépendante finale PASS. Corrections de revue: rejet du symlink sandbox/goose hors racine et surveillance de la source XDG_CONFIG_HOME effective.
close_reason: GOOSE_PATH_ROOT redirige config/data/state, OAuth reste privé, propagation et fail-closed couverts; validations ciblées et vérification indépendante PASS.

title: Aligner le fakeroot sur XDG Base Directory
description: Respecter les defaults Freedesktop quand les variables XDG sont absentes/vides et reproduire leur arborescence canonique dans le fakeroot.
design: Destination fakeroot sous HOME/.config, HOME/.local/share, HOME/.local/state, HOME/.cache; XDG_RUNTIME_DIR isolé 0700. Source Goose résolue depuis XDG_CONFIG_HOME/goose si non vide, sinon HOME/.config/goose. Un userHome injecté en test ne doit jamais lire le XDG réel sauf source explicite.
acceptance_criteria: Tooling et EvalHub appliquent defaults XDG exacts; variables vides traitées comme absentes; source XDG_CONFIG_HOME prioritaire; userHome fixture reste confinée; XDG_RUNTIME_DIR absolu/0700; HOWTO cite la spec; tests ciblés/récursifs et vérification indépendante.
close_reason: All predefined XDG criteria independently proven.

title: Implement Beads-native Loop Engineering in Goose
description: Implement a governed Loop Engineering control plane for Goose using Beads as durable state, Goose recipes for orchestration, Summon/Orchestrator for isolated or parallel agents, Skills for methodology, and an Open Plugin for lifecycle events and policy guards. Replace .loop persistence with Beads-native runs, tasks, events, state transitions, evidence references, budgets, and recovery questions.
design: Follow docs/loop-engineering/diagrams: Trigger -> Planner -> Builder -> independent Verifier -> Memory -> Manager -> Controller. Represent each run as a Beads epic/molecule; represent phases/increments as child tasks and blocking dependencies; use metadata plus bd set-state for phase/transition/verdict; use events/comments for history and evidence references. Goose recipe remains the controller and delegates specialists. Hooks are lifecycle observability and safety, fail open when Beads is unavailable, and never use .loop as source of truth.
acceptance_criteria:
AC-LE-01: No Loop Engineering runtime state is persisted under .loop; Beads is the durable control plane.
AC-LE-02: The top-level recipe creates/resumes a Beads run, models bounded tasks/dependencies, claims work before writes, and persists typed transitions and evidence.
AC-LE-03: Builder and verifier are isolated agents; independent work can be delegated in parallel where dependencies permit; controller enforces budgets/stagnation/terminal conditions.
AC-LE-04: Every phase asks phase-specific recovery questions about tools, checks, memory, failures, and newly added evidence that may change a verdict.
AC-LE-05: Goose lifecycle hooks record sanitized Beads events and block dangerous shell commands using supported hook contracts, while failing open if dependencies are unavailable.
AC-LE-06: Skills, agents, recipes, specs, eval declarations, docs, and generated tables are internally consistent and relevant deterministic tests pass.
notes: Evidence: 4 recipes valid; plugin test passed; consistency passed; recipe metadata passed; KG pipeline passed; docs HTML/PDF/report build passed. Goose emitted known non-fatal OpenTelemetry shutdown warnings during recipe validation.
close_reason: Beads-native Loop Engineering implemented and independently validated

title: Add side-effect-free Eval Hub --help mode
description:
Objective:
Add an explicit --help mode to Eval Hub so users can request usage information without accidentally starting the HTTP server or TUI.

In scope:
- Recognize --help and -h before default mode selection.
- Print the existing usage/modes/options/environment guidance to stdout.
- Exit successfully without importing or starting server, TUI, eval, report, export, browser, or benchmark modes.
- Add focused automated regression tests for both help aliases and side-effect prevention.

Out of scope:
- Redesigning CLI argument parsing or introducing a CLI dependency.
- Changing any existing mode, option, default TTY behavior, help wording beyond extraction needed for reuse, or generated dist files.
- Updating unrelated documentation, recipes, agents, eval definitions, APIs, or TUI screens.

Constraints:
- Preserve all existing CLI behavior when neither --help nor -h is supplied.
- Do not edit any file currently modified or untracked except the clean expected files named in this contract.

title: Define one end-to-end UI/API/analytics/accessibility behavior contract
description:
Objective:
Turn the unspecified cross-layer request involving UI copy, API behavior, analytics, and accessibility into one evidence-backed, implementation-ready vertical-slice contract for a single user action.

In scope:
- Identify the exact screen/component, user action, API operation, current response/error contract, analytics convention, and accessibility behavior in the target repository/specification.
- Define one user-observable state transition end to end: API outcome -> UI state and approved-copy placeholder -> accessible announcement/focus behavior -> analytics event.
- Record API compatibility and privacy constraints, including which values may be exposed to UI or analytics.
- Produce a decision table and one smallest follow-up implementation task with concrete proof paths.

Out of scope:
- Production or test code changes.
- Broad copy rewrites, API redesigns, analytics taxonomy migrations, unrelated accessibility remediation, localization rollout, visual redesign, or multiple user journeys.
- Inventing exact copy, event names/properties, API status codes, or assistive-technology behavior without governing evidence or an accountable product/accessibility decision.

Deliverable:
A repository-cited end-to-end behavior contract for exactly one user action and one primary API outcome, plus a linked implementation task. If the target product flow or repository is unavailable, record the blocker and required owner/input instead of guessing.

## Required Skills
task-framing

## Required Skills
task-framing
design: Treat this as one vertical product behavior, not four layer-based implementation tasks. First trace the existing user action through component, API boundary, response mapping, analytics instrumentation, and accessibility semantics/tests. Separate observed facts from assumptions. The contract's decision table must contain: trigger and API outcome; visible state; approved-copy reference or product-owner placeholder; accessible name/description, live-region or focus behavior where applicable; analytics trigger, canonical event/schema reference, allowed properties, and deduplication rule; privacy/security constraints; and proof. Preserve backward compatibility unless the governing spec explicitly authorizes a break. Escalate exact wording and taxonomy choices to product/analytics owners and semantic/focus choices unsupported by standards or existing patterns to the accessibility owner. Do not implement during this task.

AC-1: The target user action is bounded to one cited screen/component and one cited API operation, with current UI, API, analytics, accessibility, tests, and governing specification inventoried; proof: file/symbol/spec references and reproducible read-only search commands.
AC-2: A decision table defines one primary API outcome end to end, including externally observable API semantics, visible UI state, copy source/owner, accessible announcement or focus semantics, analytics trigger/schema/privacy/deduplication behavior, and explicit non-goals; proof: table cross-referenced to repository conventions and specification clauses.
AC-3: The API portion states compatibility, authorization, validation, error-envelope, and sensitive-data constraints without inventing unsupported status codes or fields; proof: contract/API-test references and an API compatibility checklist.
AC-4: The UI behavior remains understandable without analytics or assistive technology, and the accessibility behavior is keyboard- and screen-reader-testable without relying on visible text alone; proof: named automated accessibility/component checks plus a concise manual keyboard/screen-reader procedure appropriate to the discovered stack.
AC-5: Analytics fires only for the defined transition, follows an existing canonical schema, excludes copy text and sensitive/free-form payloads, and has a repeat/deduplication rule; proof: analytics unit/integration test plan and schema/privacy review reference.
AC-6: One claimable follow-up implementation task captures the smallest coherent vertical slice, its expected files, dependencies, falsifiable ACs, and exact discovered test commands; proof: linked Beads task ID. No production/test files are modified by this framing task; proof: git status/diff.

Evidence: the two pages contain 965 words, multiple competing entry patterns, and unexplained terms including ACs, control plane, molecule/wisp, bead, recipe, gate, subagent, and session; no end-to-end worked example maps a goal to artifacts and completion. Scope: introduce essential vocabulary just in time and move advanced concepts behind links.
acceptance_criteria: A novice golden path uses one primary action per stage; every required term is defined at first use or linked; advanced Beads and delegation concepts are visually secondary; one concrete feature example shows command, expected artifact/state, and next step through release; usability review confirms no backtracking is required.
close_reason: out-of-scope: UX progressive disclosure is a general docs improvement unrelated to loop engineering mechanics; close until a specific loop engineering UX gap is measured

title: UX-02: Repair onboarding navigation and dead-end links
description: Why: Users cannot continue from Getting Started to the promised reference material. Evidence: browser-click trials for Architecture Overview, Recipe Guide, and SDD Workflow all end at ERR_FILE_NOT_FOUND; getting-started.md and 00-index.md do not link to each other. Scope: repair or replace targets and provide bidirectional, task-oriented navigation.
acceptance_criteria: All three Next Steps resolve successfully in the built docs; Getting Started links to the workflow chooser and the workflow chooser links back to setup; a link checker covers both pages; labels describe the user task rather than only document names.
close_reason: resolved commit=60234b5: dead-links fixed (4e6caaf), overflow-x:auto (b7d27fb), slash-command preservation already in install.sh, Mermaid.js CDN injection for workflow diagrams

## 1. CANONICAL EXPECTATION FROM MATT POCOCK SKILLS

### Core Concepts (writing-great-skills/SKILL.md:15-28,42,63; GLOSSARY.md:21-97,131)

| Concept | Definition | Recipe Relevance |
|---------|-----------|------------------|
| **Model-invoked vs User-invoked** | Skills choose invocation axis: model (description kept, context load) vs user (description stripped, cognitive load) | Recipes should not over-own skill methodology; skills decide their own discoverability |
| **Progressive Disclosure** | Move reference down the ladder via context pointers; top stays legible | Recipes should load skills on-demand, not inline methodology |
| **Information Hierarchy** | Steps (primary) → In-skill reference → External reference | Recipe instructions vs delegated skill instructions |
| **Context Load vs Cognitive Load** | Model-invoked costs context; user-invoked costs human memory | Skill loading patterns in recipes |
| **Router Skill** | One user-invoked skill that indexes others | Routing tables in recipes vs skill-level routing |
| **Granularity** | Split by invocation (leading word trigger) or sequence (hide post-completion steps) | Recipe-to-skill composition boundaries |

notes:
## Loop-Engineering Evidence Ledger — Recipes Layer

### Concept Contract Reference
From bvuj.7 CLOSED:
- Flow: claim bead/assignee → pre-delegation checks → isolated maker evidence → independent review → correction/retry within 2 review BLOCK and 3 implement/verify cycles → inspect sessions before stuck retry → principal-engineer at >=2 BLOCKs → halt/create escalation bead/report user at 3 unresolved iterations → close only on checker success
- Goose summon.rs:873-1082 exposes peek/wait/cancel, 5-minute wait return, 5-second cancel abort, TTL, and no automatic retry
- Questions: counter independence/persistence, restart reconstruction, slow/stuck/failed state taxonomy, retry strategy change, escalation authority, handback payload, review-before-verification ordering

### Canonical Expectation Sources
1. orchestrator.md:98-99,112,118-119,125,135-144,178,183-190,196,218,221,230,237 — loop bounds, escalation thresholds, maker/checker
2. Goose agent.rs:68 DEFAULT_MAX_TURNS=1000, retry.rs RetryManager with attempts counter

- max_turns: 35
- No explicit retry counter or escalation to principal-engineer
**Expected vs Actual**: Expects bounded browser retry (2 attempts); actual implementation is instructional text, not code-enforced gate

### Cross-Cutting Findings

1. **Counter persistence**: No recipe tracks iteration counters across sessions. Goose agent.rs:250 RetryManager exists but recipes rely on instructional bounds. Classification: Enhancement candidate.

notes:
Synthesis from delegated research (2026-07-18):

Primary design direction:
- Keep .agents/agents/harness-judge.md short: persona, boundaries, when to invoke/not invoke, operating process, output format, and hard safety rules.
- Put the detailed checklists/questions/rubrics/calibration anchors in .agents/skills/harness-judge/SKILL.md.
- Preserve Goose/open .agents compatibility: Markdown + YAML frontmatter; agent name matches file stem; skill name matches directory; skill has metadata.version; recipes validated with goose recipe validate.

Reference-informed judge principles:
- Evidence-first: every score needs artifact path/turn/tool call/quote or explicit "not found".
- Criteria-before-verdict: score individual criteria before aggregate.
- Trajectory-aware: judge ordering, tool calls, delegation, validation, and handoff, not just final answer.
- Bias-aware: guard against verbosity, positional, sycophancy, style/self-enhancement, and circularity.
- Pairwise/layer-delta: score baseline and enhanced independently, then compare criterion-level deltas; allow positive/neutral/negative deltas.
- Reproducible: capture scenario/layer, judge model, rubric version, timestamp, files/transcripts, thresholds.

Domain additions to plan:
A Prompt/context/loop engineering:
- Add judgeability of prompt, context minimality, explicit assumptions, progressive disclosure, loop readiness level, max iterations, pause/kill criteria, escalation, evidence-friendly outputs.
B Skills:
- Add frontmatter/name/path checks, description trigger specificity, progressive disclosure, single responsibility, examples/gotchas/verification, scripts/references/assets separation, observable method steps, layer-delta usefulness.
C Agents:
- Add frontmatter/name/model checks, required sections, invoke/do-not-invoke boundaries, persona specificity, skill-loading expectations, circuit breakers, maker/checker split, no self-approval, no subagent delegation.
D Recipes:
- Add goose recipe validate hard gate, top-level field checks, parameter/subrecipe path checks, AD-001 pattern compliance, eval JSON in-session agents only, methodology locality, completion/handoff conditions.
E Frameworks:
- Add spec-to-test traceability, SDD/TDD sequence evidence, RED-GREEN-REFACTOR, GDD generation constraints/options/tradeoffs, verifier theater red flag, regression evidence.
F Orchestration:
- Add recipe->agent->skill layer discipline, Orchestration decision before delegate, non-overlapping scopes, read-only parallel/write sequenced, context isolation, synthesis not forwarding, delegation audit, circuit breakers.

Concrete sections to add/update later:
- "Common Rationalizations" section: small diff so no tests; env failure so ignore; docs close enough; summoned agents can be listed as in-session; loaded agent vs delegated agent confusion.
- "Red Flags" section: no citations, no validation command, hand-edited generated sections, AD-001 ignored, success claimed after failing validation, verifier theater.
- Numbered checklist IDs: HJ001 evidence cited; HJ002 scope preserved; HJ003 layer comparison correct; HJ004 validation considered; HJ005 generated sections untouched; expand per domain.

Validation plan before accepting edits:
- goose skills list
- python3 scripts/generate-tables.py if generated docs impacted
- python3 scripts/check-consistency.py
- node apps/kg/dist/cli.js pipeline after structural harness changes
- if recipes touched: goose recipe validate relevant file(s)
- optionally eval: node apps/eval-hub/dist/index.js --run --layers agents --subject harness-judge --ambient-goose; and skills --subjects harness-judge.

Important caveat:
- Old Goose docs URLs may redirect/404; prefer current goose-docs.ai docs and local repo invariants.

title: Eval: store Goose session ID — switch from --no-session to named sessions
description:
Currently eval runs use --no-session (ephemeral, no session ID persisted).
We added first_message_id (Anthropic API trace) + token counts as practical alternatives.

To get a real Goose session ID for post-hoc inspection:
1. Replace --no-session with --session eval-{run_id}-{eval_id}-{config}-{run_num}
2. After the run, read the session ID from the goose-home sessions directory
3. Store it in eval_run_results.goose_session_id
4. The session file at ~/.local/state/goose/sessions/ (or isolated goose-home) would then be inspectable with 'goose session list' and 'goose session inspect <id>'

Tradeoff: named sessions persist to disk (more storage), but enable full post-hoc conversation replay.
Current workaround: events.jsonl + first_message_id + token counts cover most debugging needs.
